title: Game of Thrones
note: Written by Claude for Watch Together. Moments are approximate (fraction of the runtime, in scene order). Production facts only - no spoilers beyond the episode.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – Winter Is Coming (S1E1)

items.fact: 'Winter is coming' are the words of House Stark - every great house has its own motto, and this one became the show's tagline.

cue: the things i do for love
items.fact: Jaime's line ends the pilot - the moment non-readers realised this show would not play it safe.
'Wear it like armor' - Tyrion's advice to Jon comes almost word for word from George R. R. Martin's first book.

cue: what do we say to the god of death
items.fact: Syrio's 'Not today' becomes one of Arya's guiding lines - the show calls back to it in its final season.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – You Win or You Die (S1E7)

items.fact: Cersei's line gives the episode its title - and sums up the whole series in one sentence.
Sean Bean has died in so many roles that his on-screen deaths became a running joke - this is the most famous of them.

cue: and who are you the proud lord said
items.fact: 'The Rains of Castamere' is sung here for the first time; the band The National recorded it for this episode's end credits.
This episode was written by George R. R. Martin himself - Tyrion leading the defence is straight from his book.

names: and now his watch is ended
entries.title: Game of Thrones – And Now His Watch Is Ended (S3E4)

cue: a dragon is not a slave
items.fact: Emilia Clarke learned her High Valyrian lines phonetically - the language was expanded for the show by linguist David J. Peterson.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – The Rains of Castamere (S3E9)

items.fact: Martin based the Red Wedding on two real Scottish massacres - the Black Dinner (1440) and the Glencoe massacre (1692).
George R. R. Martin told the showrunners Hodor's secret years before this episode; Kristian Nairn said he cried reading the script.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – Battle of the Bastards (S6E9)

items.fact: This was Iwan Rheon's last scene as Ramsay; the battle before it took 25 days to film with around 500 extras and 70 horses.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – The Winds of Winter (S6E10)

items.fact: Bella Ramsey's young Lyanna Mormont shames the northern lords here - Ramsey later starred in The Last of Us.
The singing soldier is Ed Sheeran - a cameo arranged because Maisie Williams is a fan.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – The Long Night (S8E3)

cue: what do we say to the god of death
items.fact: A callback to Syrio Forel's lesson in season 1's 'Lord Snow'. The battle took 55 consecutive night shoots to film.
